Admiralty Fleet Orders (AFOs)

Admiralty Fleet Orders (AFOs) (initially Admiralty Weekly Orders (AWOs)) were official instructions and notices issued by the British Admiralty to communicate decisions and requirements throughout the Royal Navy. They covered a wide range of subjects, including personnel administration, equipment, stores and shore establishments, providing a means of applying common rules and procedures across a geographically dispersed service. Their contents ranged from routine administrative changes to detailed instructions affecting the equipment and support of warships.

AFOs provide a record of how Admiralty policy was translated into practical requirements. They can help establish when changes were announced, which ships or establishments were affected, and what action was required, although an order’s publication does not necessarily establish when its instructions were implemented. Confidential Admiralty Fleet Orders (CAFOs) formed a parallel series for material requiring restricted circulation. Collections of both are preserved at The National Archives in series ADM 182.

This table was compiled by Paul Bevand of the HMS Hood Association. It is a work in progress, and coverage will be extended progressively.
